title: Public bodies the City pays, in the State Controller’s pay files
question: Do the separate public bodies that receive City money report their payroll to the State, as the City does?
finding: The State Controller files on disk are pay files, not financial statements: they list positions and pay, with no revenue or spending. 9 San Francisco public bodies in them were paid $1.70 billion by the City in fiscal 2019 to 2026; 6 have a gap. The San Francisco Community Health Authority (the State file gives its website as sfhp.org; the City ledger pays “San Francisco Health Plan”, $219.3 million in these years) lists 10 governing-board positions and no pay in 2025; in no year from 2019 to 2025 does the file hold a staff position for it. Transbay Joint Powers Authority: pay total under a fifth of its usual level in 2022 (likely a reporting error); San Francisco Unified: no report for 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025; San Francisco Community College District: no report for 2023, 2024, 2025; Metropolitan Transportation Commission: no report for 2019; Golden Gate Bridge Highway and Transportation District: no report for 2020.
how: Sums by employer and year from the 76 State Controller raw exports (the 20XX_<entity>.zip files), employers in San Francisco County, set against City payment-table totals for the payee spellings listed in the script, leaving out payments a body makes from its own funds held in the City treasury (department codes CCD and USD). A year is missing when the export for that year has no row for the employer.
limits: Whether a missing year is a late report or no report cannot be told from the export, which is what was saved on 17 November 2026. A health plan’s staff may be employed by a separate entity that does not report to the State Controller. City payments to a transit district or a court are for services and shared projects, not payroll, so the two columns are context for each other, not a ratio. Nothing here suggests money is missing.

rows.note: positions listed with no pay in every year
pay total under a fifth of its usual level in 2022 (likely a reporting error)

Golden Gate Bridge Highway and Transportation District
